title: Choose the approach for ticket triage
context: Triage must classify, attach shipments and escalate, inside the client's AWS account in the EU, run by a small Python team for under 0.04 USD a ticket.

anchors.1: Fails one or more must scenarios in the spike
anchors.3: Meets them with workarounds we would have to maintain
anchors.5: Meets all of them with the framework's own features

criteria.name: Team can build and run it

anchors.1: Nobody on the team has used it; no local support
anchors.3: One engineer has used it; training needed
anchors.5: The team runs it in production today

anchors.1: We build tracing, retries and approval ourselves
Preview features on the critical path
anchors.5: GA over a year with a stable API

knockouts.name: Runs fully inside the client's EU AWS account

options.name: Fixed workflow with one model call
options.summary: A queue worker calls the order API, then one structured-output model call returns queue and reason. No agent loop.

fit.evidence: Spike SPK-1 scored 91.5% queue accuracy and 25 of 25 escalations with one call

team.evidence: Plain Python and boto3, which the team ships today

cost.evidence: Measured 0.011 USD per ticket in SPK-1

ops.evidence: Retries and the confidence gate are 60 lines of our own code; tracing through OpenTelemetry

risk.evidence: Bedrock Converse API has been GA since 2024

fit.evidence: Meets FR-1 to FR-3 in the spike; FR-4 needs a second call

team.evidence: Team wrote the spike in two days

cost.evidence: Token counts from the spike trace give 0.011 USD

ops.evidence: Approval and retry are hand-written but small

risk.evidence: No preview dependency on the path

options.name: LangGraph agent with tools
options.summary: A graph with classify, lookup and review nodes; interrupt for the human gate; SQLite or Postgres checkpointer.

fit.evidence: Interrupts and checkpointing cover QS-2 and QS-6 directly

team.evidence: One engineer has built with it; the other has not

cost.evidence: Agent loop used 2.9 calls per ticket in the spike, 0.034 USD

ops.evidence: Interrupt, retry policy and LangSmith or OpenTelemetry traces are built in

risk.evidence: 1.x is GA; API moved between 0.x and 1.0

team.evidence: Needs a week of ramp-up for one engineer

cost.evidence: About three times the baseline's cost per ticket

ops.evidence: Built in, though the checkpointer adds a database to run

options.name: Strands agent on Bedrock AgentCore
options.summary: Strands agent with tools behind AgentCore Gateway, hosted on AgentCore Runtime.

fit.evidence: Meets the scenarios; human gate through an interrupt hook

team.evidence: Nobody on the team has run AgentCore

cost.evidence: Runtime and gateway charges on top of tokens: 0.052 USD estimated

ops.evidence: Tracing and identity are built in

risk.evidence: Runtime is GA; Policy and Evaluations are under a year old

fit.evidence: Meets the must scenarios in the docs; not spiked

risk.evidence: Young services on the critical path

options.name: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET)
options.summary: Agent with approval-required functions on Azure.

change_our_mind: FR-4 (suggested reply) becomes a must: a second step and a review loop favour the graph
Queue accuracy on live traffic falls under 88% for two weeks
More than three tools are needed per ticket
